architecture_decisions.recommendation: Replaced markdown-it with markdown-exit as the core markdown processing library
architecture_decisions.rationale: markdown-exit provides better handling of code block escaping and is maintained by the same ecosystem. This reduces maintenance overhead and improves reliability of code rendering in slides. The change aligns with upstream updates in unplugin-vue-markdown which also migrated to markdown-exit.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated API naming from markdown-it to markdown-exit terminology while maintaining compatibility
architecture_decisions.rationale: Changed configuration option names from `markdownItSetup` to `markdownSetup` and `markdownItOptions` to `markdownOptions` to reflect the new library while maintaining similar API surface. This provides a clear migration path and reduces confusion for users.
alternatives_considered: Keep old API names with new implementation
Use adapter pattern to maintain backward compatibility

architecture_decisions.recommation: Updated TypeScript imports and type definitions from MarkdownIt to MarkdownExit
architecture_decisions.rationale: Ensures type safety across the codebase by updating all type imports and annotations. Added @ts-expect-error comments where necessary for compatibility with existing plugins that expect MarkdownItAsync types, since markdown-exit is API-compatible but has different type definitions.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Implemented custom escapeHtml function to replace markdown-it's utility
architecture_decisions.rationale: markdown-exit doesn't export the same escapeHtml utility as markdown-it, so a simple replacement function was created. This ensures HTML escaping continues to work in the index.html generation without adding unnecessary dependencies.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated markdown-it-escape-code plugin to handle async rendering
architecture_decisions.rationale: markdown-exit uses async rendering by default, so the code_inline renderer rule needed to be updated to async/await pattern. This ensures the v-pre attribute continues to be added to inline code elements for Vue compatibility.

implementation_summary:
The implementation replaces the markdown-it library with markdown-exit to improve code block escaping reliability and reduce maintenance overhead. This was a coordinated change that required updates across multiple layers of the application: dependency management, type definitions, API surface, and internal utilities.

The migration follows a systematic approach: first updating all imports and type annotations from MarkdownIt to MarkdownExit, then adjusting the configuration API to reflect the new library while maintaining backward compatibility through similar naming patterns. The escapeHtml utility function had to be reimplemented since markdown-exit doesn't export this helper, demonstrating a thoughtful trade-off between dependency reduction and functionality preservation.

Notably, the change was coordinated with an update to unplugin-vue-markdown v30.0.0, which also migrated to markdown-exit, ensuring compatibility across the ecosystem. The TypeScript handling shows careful attention to detail with @ts-expect-error comments for plugin compatibility, acknowledging that while the APIs are compatible, the type definitions differ. This migration improves the robustness of code rendering in slides while maintaining all existing functionality through careful API design and implementation.
